biography: Norberto Kröning Correa, a name synonymous with audacious flair and raw speed in the Brazilian Copa Fusca scene, hails from the vibrant favelas of Rio de Janeiro. Growing up amidst the cacophony of samba and the rumble of modified engines, Norberto's passion for racing ignited early. He began tearing up the streets in a beat-up, inherited Volkswagen Beetle, honing his skills in impromptu, high-stakes races under the watchful eyes of the community. His raw talent caught the attention of a local racing team owner during one particularly daring street race, leading to his official debut in the Copa Fusca series. His defining moment came at Interlagos in 2021, when, after starting last due to a mechanical failure in qualifying, he carved his way through the field with a series of breathtaking overtakes, ultimately claiming a stunning victory. Now, at 34, Norberto is at the peak of his career, a flamboyant veteran battling for championships while remaining true to his roots.
drivingStyle: Norberto's driving style is a captivating blend of aggression and precision. He's known for his late-braking maneuvers and fearless corner entries, often pushing the limits of grip to gain an advantage. He possesses an uncanny ability to sense the car's balance, allowing him to make split-second adjustments and extract maximum performance from his machine. While some criticize his aggressive tendencies, his undeniable speed and race craft make him a formidable opponent. He manages tire wear reasonably well, but his eagerness to attack often leads to a drop in performance late in races.

careerHighlight: Winning the 2021 Interlagos race after starting last due to a mechanical failure. He overtook nearly every car on track in a dazzling display of skill and determination, solidifying his reputation as a rising star.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the championship-deciding race in 2022 while leading. A mechanical failure sent him spinning into the wall, costing him the title and leaving him devastated.
